title: Metre - Wikipedia
snippet: The metre (or meter in US spelling; symbol: m) is the base unit of length in the International System of Units (SI). Since 2019, the metre has been defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1 299 792 458 of a second, where the second is defined by a hyperfine transition frequency of caesium. title: SI Unit of Length Metre and Its Modern Definition
snippet: Sep 13, 2026 · Conclusion The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length, but its modern definition represents much more than a simple measurement convention. title: SI base unit: metre (m) - BIPM
snippet: SI base unit: metre (m) The metre, symbol m, is the SI unit of length. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum c to be 299 792 458 when expressed in the unit m s–1, where the second is defined in terms of the caesium frequency ΔνCs. This definition implies the exact relation c = 299 792 458 m s –1.
